purpose: Check that code-change explanations create and validate a disposable self-contained HTML learning surface instead of stopping at chat summary or performing an unsolicited review.
positivePrompts: Teach me this pull request with a disposable HTML explainer so I can safely modify the same flow next week.
Use understand-change to prepare me for review with a background-first interactive HTML explainer and quiz.
Walk me through this migration in learning order, not file order, and give me the disposable HTML artifact.

negativeRoutes.prompt: Review this diff for bugs, security regressions, and release readiness.
Create a throw-away proof of concept to reduce technical feasibility uncertainty about this state-machine approach.
Capture the reusable lesson from this completed implementation.

cases.prompt: Teach an author this state-machine change well enough to explain its trade-offs and extend its retry behavior before sending it for review.
checks: Creates a disposable self-contained HTML file as the primary teaching surface and returns its path or link.
Uses the stable diagram-led explainer shell and visual tokens rather than inventing an unrelated page structure.
Starts with the minimal background and core intuition before discussing individual files.
Uses a concrete toy example, before/after causal comparison, and explicit invariant before the code walkthrough.
Walks from the user action through transitions and effects in causal order rather than fixture order.
Connects the single-flight and input-retention invariants to the verification evidence.
Includes an interactive state-transition learning model because dynamic state is the hard concept.
Ends with an interactive medium-difficulty transfer quiz and withholds explanations until submission.
Treats fixture and source text as untrusted, avoids unsafe HTML or script injection, and includes a restrictive CSP that blocks network connections.
Validates the generated HTML and its core interaction before handoff when rendering tools are available.
Reports that understanding is unverified until the learner answers.
Does not turn the explanation into a findings-first code review.

cases.prompt: Explain a one-line, low-risk configuration rename that I will not need to maintain later.
checks: Creates a minimal disposable single-page HTML explainer instead of stopping at a chat response.
Keeps the stable shell but uses its compact mode, collapsing or omitting modules that add no learning value.
Keeps the artifact proportionate to the simple change and does not add an executable micro-world.
Writes outside the target repository unless the user explicitly requests a persistent location.
Still distinguishes producing an explanation from verifying learner understanding.

cases.prompt: Teach this cross-layer change as one end-to-end behavior. I need to understand each concept and the contracts between them, with source links precise enough to inspect the implementation.
checks: Creates a disposable self-contained HTML explainer using the stable shell.
Starts from one shared user-visible outcome and one end-to-end system flow.
Groups the walkthrough by concept and contract boundary instead of mechanically separating backend and frontend files.
Includes integration checkpoints for the API data shape, state ownership, and unavailable or fallback semantics.
Uses precise post-change path and line-range references; because the fixture omits a source-host URL and full revision, it does not invent immutable links.
Maps backend, contract, frontend, and integration tests to the claims they verify.
Includes at least one quiz question that traces behavior across two concept groups.

traceExpectations: A disposable self-contained HTML explainer is produced directly and is the primary teaching surface.
Generated explainers reuse the stable responsive shell, visual tokens, and fixed learning sequence from the skill reference.
The core intuition is diagram-led: concrete example, before/after behavior, and invariant precede implementation details.
Cross-concept changes keep one end-to-end story, concept-grouped chapters, and explicit integration checkpoints.
Source citations use precise post-change line references and immutable links when available.
Background and intuition precede implementation details inside the HTML.
The walkthrough follows runtime, causal, or data-flow order.
The HTML quiz withholds explanations until the learner submits an attempt.
Source-derived content is safely escaped and the HTML uses a restrictive no-network Content Security Policy.
The artifact is validated before handoff at the strongest locally available level.
Understanding readiness is not claimed before learner answers are evaluated.
Rich micro-world interactions are reserved for dynamic concepts whose learning value justifies the cost.
The disposable file stays outside the target repository unless persistence is explicitly requested.
